- **Main change:** FY2025 makes AMD’s AI growth risks more concrete—export restrictions caused actual inventory charges, while customer infrastructure, financing and faster product transitions receive more attention. Most changes expand existing exposures rather than establish entirely new risks. Both complete original annual sections were reviewed. [S1] [S2]

- **Export controls and tariffs — expanded disclosure:**
  - April 2025 MI308 licensing restrictions resulted in approximately **$800 million of Q2 inventory and related charges**. AMD subsequently obtained some licenses, resumed shipments and reversed approximately **$360 million in Q4**.
  - Officials’ expectation of receiving **15% of licensed MI308 China revenue** was disclosed, but AMD stated that no regulation establishing that requirement had been published.
  - Added detail covers AI Diffusion Rule replacement uncertainty, tariffs affecting data-center investment, and Entity List affiliate restrictions whose enforcement was planned to be suspended. These update an existing export-control risk. [S1] [S2]

- **AI infrastructure and commercial commitments — expanded risks plus a new dedicated risk factor:**
  - Customer demand may be constrained by data-center construction delays, power availability, insufficient capital and requests for deferred payments.
  - A new standalone factor addresses AMD’s capacity-purchase agreements, guarantees and leases supporting customer or partner infrastructure.
  - No equivalent infrastructure-support obligation disclosure appears in the complete FY2024 section. This is newly disclosed specificity—not proof that all guarantee or counterparty exposure began in FY2025; those broader exposures already existed. [S1] [S2]

- **Competition — consolidated and changed, not eliminated:** Separate Intel and Nvidia factors were rewritten into the broader competition discussion. FY2025 adds the September 2025 Nvidia–Intel partnership as a potential source of pricing pressure and lost opportunities. Arm competition and customers developing competing products remain. This is not an identical-wording relocation. [S1] [S2]

- **Supply and product execution — expanded:** AMD now describes an industry-wide memory shortage and rising memory prices. Shorter launch cycles, overlapping product generations and longer manufacturing lead times increase demand-forecasting and inventory-mismatch risks. These elaborate existing supply and product-transition exposures. [S1] [S2]

- **ZT Systems — pending-closing disclosure removed; integration risk retained:** FY2025 states that the acquisition closed in **March 2025**. The specific pending-approval/closing risk and associated **$300 million termination-fee disclosure** are absent from the complete FY2025 risk section. General acquisition, integration and divestiture risks remain; divestiture language adds potential post-closing purchase-price adjustments. [S1] [S2]

- **Other notable changes:**
  - Cybersecurity adds internal AI-system vulnerabilities, human error and third-party credentials; AI regulation expressly may delay or halt customer deployments. [S1] [S2]
  - Tax language discusses **January 2026** OECD relief as generally favorable, subject to country adoption. NOL and specific tax-loss limitation wording is dropped; that does not establish that the underlying tax exposure disappeared. [S1] [S2]
  - Immigration restrictions, geopolitical developments and gray-market warranty/diversion risks receive more detail. Debt covenant disclosure adds 2026/2028 notes. Repurchase authorization/remaining capacity changes from **$12 billion/$4.7 billion** to **$14 billion/$9.4 billion**. [S1] [S2]

- **Management context:** AMD continues to describe significant AI demand but an uncertain adoption trajectory. Foundry dependence, manufacturing yields, customer concentration, IP protection and responsible AI remain core risks. The interpretation is greater specificity around executing AI growth—not a wholesale replacement of the risk inventory. [S1] [S2]

- **Comparison basis and amendment treatment:**
  - **FY2024:** December 31, 2023–December 28, 2024; original **10-K**, accession **0000002488-25-000012**. [S1]
  - **FY2025:** December 29, 2024–December 27, 2025; original **10-K**, accession **0000002488-26-000018**. [S2]
  - The supplied amendment treatment specifies that AMD’s FY2025 **10-K/A corrects MD&A and does not replace Item 1A**. Therefore, the original FY2025 10-K—not the amendment—is the annual risk-comparison source. Amendment text and accession were not supplied, so its precise correction details cannot be independently established here.

changes.rationale: Export/trade: existing exposure expanded with April 2025 MI308 licensing, $800m Q2 charges and $360m Q4 reversal; 15% revenue expectation not a published rule; AI Diffusion replacement uncertainty, tariffs and Entity List affiliate rule suspension. New events within existing risk.
AI demand and climate infrastructure: adds data-center construction, energy/capacity and customer capital/deferred-payment constraints; existing power/water risks expanded, not wholly new exposure.

New dedicated customer/partner infrastructure commercial commitment risk: capacity purchase agreements, financial guarantees and leases and potential payment upon counterparty distress. No equivalent infrastructure-support obligation disclosure found anywhere in complete FY2024 section; existing Xilinx guarantees, supplier commitments and factoring risks mean not all guarantee/counterparty exposure is new.

Competition: separate Intel and Nvidia subjects consolidated and reworded in competition, not removed or identical relocation. Adds September 2025 Nvidia-Intel partnership example; Arm/customer competition persists. Government incentive language persists under export controls with CHIPS example dropped.

Product transitions/order forecasting: shorter launch cycles, concurrent generations, customer inventory reductions and longer manufacturing lead times expand existing product delay and inventory mismatch risks.
Supply/macro: reports current industry-wide memory shortage and price increases, expanding existing limited-supplier and cost risk; tariffs and retaliation emphasized.

Specific pending ZT acquisition closing/approval and $300m termination-fee disclosure absent throughout complete FY2025 section; acquisition completed March 2025. This removes pending-closing disclosure only, not integration or general acquisition/divestiture exposure.
M&A: ZT now completed, integration benefits remain uncertain; divestiture risks generalized from ZT-specific plan with post-closing purchase-price adjustments added.

Cyber/AI regulation: adds human error, third-party credentials/untrusted assets and internal AI systems vulnerability; AI regulation now expressly may delay/halt customer deployments. Existing AI cyber and responsible-use risks predate FY2025.

Tax: January 2026 OECD side-by-side safe harbors/exemption described as generally favorable but country adoption required. DTA description drops NOL reference and specific loss-limitation paragraph; no inference tax exposure extinguished.

Global/personnel: adds immigration control hiring/employment consequences, public perception of US government and Venezuela conflict; international sales 66% to 67%. Existing geopolitical/talent exposure expanded.

Other updates: gray-market pricing misuse, unauthorized warranties and diversion controls expanded; notes list adds 2026/2028 maturities; factoring repurchase warning omitted but factoring remains; stock volatility drivers broaden and repurchase authorization/availability update $12bn/$4.7bn to $14bn/$9.4bn.
